title: Josh Korley, GStat – Josh Korley
text: Josh Korley, GStat Biostatistics · Trial methodology · Digital biomarkers Statistical methods for complex biomedical evidence. I am Josh Korley, a Biostatistics PhD student developing methods for complex temporal, longitudinal, and time-to-event biomedical data. My work brings together adaptive clinical trials, functional and distributional data analysis, Bayesian latent-state and survival modeling, and neurostatistics, with applications to wearable-derived digital biomarkers, neuroimaging, aging, Alzheimer’s disease, and drug development. Explore my projects ↗ View scholarly work LinkedIn Google Scholar ResearchGate ORCID GitHub Email Current focus Neurostatistics · Digital Biomarkers Adaptive Trials · Bayesian Methods Credential ASA GStat ↗ Josh Korley, GStat Biostatistics PhD student · USC Google Scholar ResearchGate ORCID Experience Research Assistant USC PhD Biostatistics Intern, Cardiovascular & Neuroscience Bristol Myers Squibb Master’s Computational Statistician Intern, Neuroscience Eli Lilly & Company Research Assistant ASPIRE Junior Scholar Fellow SmartState Center Graduate Student Instructor WMU Research & Teaching Assistant University of Ghana Adaptive clinical trials • Functional and distributional data • Bayesian latent-state and survival methods • Neurostatistics and Alzheimer’s disease • Adaptive clinical trials • Functional and distributional data • Bayesian latent-state and survival methods • Neurostatistics and Alzheimer’s disease • Academic foundation Education View full education details ↗ 2025 to present PhD in Biostatistics USC Doctoral research in adaptive trials, functional and distributional data, Bayesian latent-state and survival methods, and neurostatistics. Summer 2025 Graduate Practicum in Biostatistics UConn Biopharmaceutical Summer Academy with training in adaptive design, estimands, multiplicity, clinical-data standards, and trial simulation. 2023 to 2025 MS in Statistics WMU Graduate Certificate in Biostatistics and thesis research in causal-survival modeling for prostate cancer. 2018 to 2022 BSc in Mathematical Science University of Ghana Actuarial Science concentration. Research profile Methods shaped by the evidence and the decision. Research on how complex evidence can be used without losing its timing, uncertainty, heterogeneity, or clinical meaning. Across pharmaceutical and academic research, I study how trial adaptations, latent temporal states, survival outcomes, and wearable or neuroimaging measurements can be analyzed without losing their scientific meaning. The goal is methodology that is rigorous enough for statistical research and useful enough for biomedical decisions. 01 Adaptive clinical trials Bayesian and frequentist designs for interim learning, sample-size re-estimation, enrichment, estimands, and decisions to continue, modify, or stop a trial. 02 Functional and distributional data Methods for wearable-derived digital biomarkers that preserve daily timing, rhythm, intensity, variability, and distributional shape. 03 Bayesian latent-state and survival methods Hidden and semi-Markov models, competing risks, recurrent events, interval censoring, and informative observation processes for complex temporal and time-to-event data. 04 Neurostatistics and Alzheimer’s disease Statistical methods for neuroimaging, cognition, disease progression, genomics, and heterogeneity in aging and Alzheimer’s disease research. title: Teaching – Josh Korley
text: Teaching Teaching and mentorship Making statistical ideas clear, useful, and rigorous. My teaching spans introductory statistics, business statistics, probability, R programming, actuarial science, and quantitative research mentorship. WMU Graduate Student Instructor · Department of Statistics · August 2023 to April 2025 Led laboratory sessions, recitations, office hours, and applied demonstrations for more than 100 undergraduate students per semester. Co-developed instructional materials and laboratory modules with an emphasis on clarity, organization, and reproducible analysis. Instructor STAT 1600 · Discovery With Data Descriptive statistics, inference, data exploration, hypothesis testing, and introductory regression. Tutor STAT 2160 · Business Statistics Statistical reasoning and applied analysis for decision-making in business settings. Tutor STAT 3620 · Probability Combinatorics, discrete and continuous distributions, and foundations of probability theory. Instructor support STAT 2600 · R Statistical Programming and Computing Data workflows, reproducible programming, visualization, and statistical computing in R. University of Ghana Teaching Assistant · Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science · October 2022 to December 2023 Delivered tutorials, targeted review sessions, and academic support in statistics, probability, and actuarial science. Introduced R and Python assignments to strengthen reproducible data analysis. Statistics STAT 111 · Introduction to Statistics Descriptive methods, statistical reasoning, and foundational data analysis. Probability STAT 221 · Introduction to Statistics and Probability I Probability concepts, random variables, distributions, and introductory inference. Statistical theory STAT 333 · Statistical Inference Estimation, testing, and theoretical foundations for statistical inference. Actuarial science ACTU 605 · Actuarial Mathematics Quantitative methods for contingent payments and actuarial risk calculations. Actuarial science ACTU 405 · Actuarial Economics Economic reasoning and financial concepts for actuarial applications. Actuarial science ACTU 345 · Actuarial Statistics Statistical tools, modeling principles, and probability methods for actuarial work. Research mentorship Support beyond the classroom PhD dissertation support in mental health, May 2025. Guided confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling for resilience and mental health outcomes, including data preparation, interpretation, and reporting in R. Graduate dissertation support, March 2024 to May 2025. Advised on quantitative study design, statistical diagnostics, natural language analysis, and dissertation reporting.

title: Projects – Josh Korley
text: Projects Project portfolio A focused research program, organized by purpose. My work develops statistical methods for complex temporal, longitudinal, and time-to-event biomedical data. Each project below has one primary home so the portfolio is easy to follow, while the tags show the supporting methods without duplicating the work. Four connected research themes Design · measurement · states · outcomes 01 Adaptive clinical trials Bayesian and frequentist designs for interim learning, sample-size re-estimation, enrichment, estimands, and decisions to continue, modify, or stop a trial. 02 Functional and distributional data Methods for wearable-derived digital biomarkers that preserve daily timing, rhythm, intensity, variability, and distributional shape. 03 Bayesian latent-state and survival methods Hidden and semi-Markov models, competing risks, recurrent events, interval censoring, and informative observation processes for temporal and time-to-event data. 04 Neurostatistics and Alzheimer’s disease Statistical methods for neuroimaging, cognition, disease progression, genomics, and heterogeneity in aging and Alzheimer’s disease research. Methodological development Neurostatistics and digital biomarkers Current research programs Earlier clinical and population research 01 · Methodological development Methods for trials, events, and changing states Primary methodological projects focused on valid decisions, interpretable effects, and complex observation processes. Adaptive clinical trials Bristol Myers Squibb · May to August 2026 Adaptive Clinical-Trial Design and Sample-Size Re-estimation A simulation-based comparison of fixed and adaptive design strategies for making efficient, statistically valid decisions during clinical development. Methods and scope Fixed designs, group sequential monitoring, sample-size re-estimation, hybrid strategies, adaptive enrichment, Type I error, power, expected enrollment, bias, and robustness to design assumptions. Adaptive trials Simulation Drug development Recurrent-event methodology Independent methodological research · 2025 to present Orthogonal Estimation of Recurrent Event Treatment Effects with Terminal Events An estimand-driven framework for recurrent clinical outcomes when death or another terminal event changes how long recurrent events can be observed. Methods and scope Survival-standardized estimands, influence-function-based inference, covariate adjustment, analytic variance estimation, and simulation under covariate-adaptive randomization. Recurrent events Causal inference Clinical trials View project ↗ Related foundational work ↗ Survival methodology USC · 2025 Robust Survival Estimation under Interval Censoring A simulation and applied assessment of distribution-free, parametric, and Bayesian approaches to survival estimation under interval censoring. Methods and scope Turnbull nonparametric maximum likelihood estimation, expectation-maximization, Weibull accelerated failure time models, Bayesian accelerated failure time models, integrated squared error, and Brier scores. Interval censoring Bayesian survival Simulation Read preprint ↗ Bayesian latent-state modeling USC · Manuscript in preparation Covariate-Dependent Hidden Markov Modeling of Virus Activity Dynamics A flexible latent-state framework for characterizing changes in virus activity using mosquito abundance and social media signals. Methods and scope Covariate-dependent transition probabilities, hidden-state inference, temporal dynamics, mosquito abundance, and auxiliary population signals. Hidden Markov models Bayesian modeling Temporal data 02 · Neurostatistics and digital biomarkers Signals of brain, behavior, and aging Projects that preserve timing and heterogeneity in neuroimaging, wearable, circadian, and cognitive-aging data. Neuroimaging and aging National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center data · 2025 to present Timing of First Neuroimaging in Alzheimer’s Disease A competing-risk investigation of when participants receive their first magnetic resonance imaging or positron emission tomography scan, with death before imaging treated as a competing event. Methods and scope Cause-specific accelerated failure time models, Cox models with time-varying effects, cumulative incidence profiles, subgroup trajectories, and hierarchical extensions. Alzheimer’s disease Neuroimaging Competing risks View project ↗ ADMRI-Timing tool ↗ Presentation slides ↗ Functional and distributional data USC · 2025 to present Wearable Activity Patterns and Cognitive Impairment Research on how the timing, intensity, variability, and distributional shape of daily physical activity relate to cognitive impairment among older adults in the National Health and Aging Trends Study. Methods and scope Functional data analysis, local distributional summaries, covariate-adjusted modeling, sensitivity analysis, and wearable-derived digital biomarkers beyond total activity counts. Cognitive aging Digital biomarkers Functional data Circadian and cardiac signals Collaboration with the University of Warwick · 2025 to present Latent-State Modeling of Circadian Patterns in 24-Hour Electrocardiogram Signals Subject-specific modeling of circadian rhythm disruption and cardiac risk using 24-hour electrocardiogram recordings from the MUSIC cohort. Methods and scope Bayesian hidden Markov models, semi-Markov models, transition-probability summaries, latent-state features, and survival outcomes. Hidden Markov models Electrocardiogram Circadian rhythms Wearable-derived digital phenotypes ASPIRE-funded research · USC · Starting August 2026 Fitbit-Derived Circadian Digital Phenotypes in Cardiology, Alzheimer’s Disease, and Related Dementias Research on wearable-derived activity, heart-rate, sleep-wake, and circadian signals as digital phenotypes of cognitive and functional change in aging and related dementias. Methods and scope Functional and longitudinal data analysis, circadian feature extraction, Bayesian hidden and semi-Markov models, and associations between temporal patterns and cognition.
